source_text: Δοκεῖ δή μοι παρακηκοέναι τινῶν ὁ Κέλσος περὶ τῆς διανεμήσεως τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς μυστικωτέρων λόγων, ὧν ἐφάπτεται μέν πως καὶ ἡ Ἑλληνικὴ ἱστορία, εἰσαγαγοῦσά τινας τῶν νομιζομένων θεῶν περὶ τῆς Ἀττικῆς πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἡμιλλῆσθαι, ποιοῦσα δὲ παρὰ τοῖς ποιηταῖς τινας τῶν λεγομένων θεῶν ὁμολογεῖν τινας τόπους οἰκειοτέρους αὐτοῖς. καὶ ἡ βαρβαρικὴ δὲ ἱστορία καὶ μάλιστα ἡ Αἰγυπτίων τοιαῦτά τινα ἐμφαίνει περὶ τοῦ μερισμοῦ τῶν τῆς Αἰγύπτου καλουμένων νομῶν, λέγουσα ὅτι ἡ λαχοῦσα τὴν Σάϊν Ἀθηνᾶ ἡ αὐτὴ ἔχει καὶ τὴν Ἀττικήν. Αἰγυπτίων δὲ οἱ λόγιοι μυρία ὅσα τοιαῦτα φήσουσιν, οὐκ οἶδα δ᾿ εἰ καὶ Ἰουδαίους συμπαραλαμβάνοντες καὶ τὴν χώραν αὐτῶν τῇ πρός τινα διανεμήσει. ἀλλὰ περὶ μὲν τῶν ἔξω τοῦ θείου λόγου λεγομένων εἰς ταῦτα ἅλις ἐπὶ τοῦ παρόντος. φαμὲν δ᾿ ὅτι ὁ καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς προφήτης τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ γνήσιος θεράπων αὐτοῦ Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῇ τοῦ Δευτερονομίου ᾠδῇ ἐκτίθεται περὶ τοῦ μερισμοῦ τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς τοιαῦτα λέγων· „ὅτε διεμέριζεν ὁ ὕψιστος ἔθνη, ὡς διέσπειρεν υἱοὺς Ἀδὰμ, ἔστησεν ὅρια ἐθνῶν κατὰ ἀριθμὸν ἀγγέλων θεοῦ, καὶ ἐγενήθη μερὶς κυρίου λαὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰακὼβ, σχοίνισμα κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ Ἰσραήλ.“ τὰ δὲ περὶ τῆς διανεμήσεως τῶν ἐθνῶν ὁ αὐτὸς Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ ἐπιγεγραμμένῳ βιβλίῳ Γένεσις ἐν ἱστορίας τρόπῳ φησὶν οὕτως· „καὶ ἦν πᾶσα ἡ γῆ χεῖλος ἓν, καὶ φωνὴ μία πᾶσι. καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κινῆσαι αὐτοὺς ἀπ᾿ ἀνατολῶν εὗρον πεδίον ἐν γῇ Σενναὰρ, καὶ κατῴκησαν ἐκεῖ“· καὶ μετ᾿ ὀλίγα· „κατέβη, φησὶ, κύριος ἰδεῖν τὴν πόλιν καὶ τὸν πύργον, ὃν ᾠκοδόμησαν οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων. καὶ εἶπε κύριος· ἰδοὺ γένος ἓν καὶ χεῖλος ἓν πάντων· καὶ τοῦτο ἤρξαντο ποιῆσαι, καὶ νῦν οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν πάντα, ὅσα ἂν ἐπιθῶνται ποιεῖν· δεῦτε καὶ καταβάντες συγχέωμεν ἐκεῖ τὴν γλῶσσαν αὐτῶν. ἵνα μὴ ἀκούσωσιν ἕκαστος τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ. καὶ διέσπειρεν αὐτοὺς κύριος ἐκεῖθεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐπαύσαντο οἰκοδομοῦντες τὴν πόλιν καὶ τὸν πύργον. διὰ τοῦτο ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Σύγχυσις, ὅτι ἐκεῖ συνέχεε κύριος ὁ θεὸς τὰ χείλη πάσης τῆς γῆς, κἀκεῖθεν διέσπειρεν αὐτοὺς κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.“ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐπιγεγραμμένῃ δὲ Σολομῶντος Σοφίᾳ περὶ τῆς σοφίας καὶ τῶν κατὰ τὴν σύγχυσιν τῶν διαλέκτων, ἐν ᾗ γεγένηται ὁ μερισμὸς τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, γῆς. τοιαῦτα περὶ τῆς σοφίας εἴρηται· „αὕτη καὶ ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ πονηρίας ἐθνῶν συγχυθέντων ἔγνω τὸν δίκαιον, καὶ ἐφύλαξεν αὐτὸν ἄμεμπτον τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τέκνου σπλάγχνοις ἰσχυρὸν ἐφύλαξε.“ πολὺς δ᾿ ὁ λόγος καὶ μυστικὸς ὁ περὶ τούτων, ᾧ ἁρμόζει τό· „μυστήριον βασιλέως κρύπτειν καλόν“· ἵνα μὴ εἰς τὰς τυχούσας ἀκοὰς ὁ περὶ ψυχῶν οὐκ ἐκ μετενσωματώσεως εἰς σῶμα ἐνδουμένων λόγος ῥιπτῆται, μηδὲ τὰ ἅγια διδῶται „τοῖς κυσὶ,“ μηδ᾿ οἱ μαργαρῖται παραβάλλωνται χοίροις. ἀσεβὲς γὰρ τὸ τοιοῦτο, προδοσίαν περιέχον τῶν ἀποῤῥήτων τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ σοφίας λογίων, περὶ ἧς καλῶς γέγραπται· „εἰς κακότεχνον ψυχὴν οὐκ εἰσελεύσεται σοφία οὐδὲ κατοικήσει ἐν σώματι κατάχρεῳ ἁμαρτίας.“ ἀρκεῖ δὲ τὰ κεκρυμμένως ὡς ἐν ἱστορίας τρόπῳ εἰρημένα κατὰ τὸν τῆς ἱστορίας παραστῆσαι τρόπον, ἵν᾿ οἱ δυνάμενοι ἑαυτοῖς ἐπεξεργάσωνται τὰ κατὰ τὸν τόπον.
thought_title: Moses on the dividing of the nations
pass_a_gloss: It seems (δοκέω) to me that Celsus has misheard (παρακούω) certain more mystical teachings (μυστικώτερος λόγος) about the distribution (διανέμησις) of the things on earth, which Greek history (Ἑλληνικὴ ἱστορία) also touches (ἐφάπτομαι) in some way, bringing in some of the supposed gods (νομιζόμενοι θεοί) as having contended (ἁμιλλάομαι) with one another about Attica, and making, in the poets, some of the so-called gods agree (ὁμολογέω) that certain places are more their own (οἰκειότερος). And barbarian history, especially that of the Egyptians, shows such things about the division (μερισμός) of the so-called nomes (νομός) of Egypt, saying that Athena who obtained by lot (λαγχάνω) Sais is the same who has Attica too. The learned (λόγιοι) of the Egyptians will say countless such things; I do not know whether also including (συμπαραλαμβάνω) the Jews and their land in the distribution to someone. But about things said outside the divine word (θεῖος λόγος) on this, enough for now. We say that the prophet of God among us and his genuine servant (γνήσιος θεράπων) Moses in the song (ᾠδή) of Deuteronomy sets out about the division of things on earth, saying: 'When the Most High (ὕψιστος) divided (διαμερίζω) nations, as he scattered (διασπείρω) sons of Adam, he set boundaries (ὅρια) of nations according to the number of angels of God (κατὰ ἀριθμὸν ἀγγέλων θεοῦ), and his people Jacob became the Lord's portion (μερίς), Israel the measured lot (σχοίνισμα) of his inheritance (κληρονομία).' The same Moses in the book entitled Genesis says about the distribution of the nations in the manner of history (ἐν ἱστορίας τρόπῳ): 'And all the earth was one lip (χεῖλος), and one voice (φωνή) for all. And it happened in their moving (κινέω) from the east (ἀπ᾿ ἀνατολῶν) they found a plain in the land of Sennaar and dwelt there'; and a little after: 'The Lord came down to see the city and the tower which the sons of men built. And the Lord said: behold one race and one lip of all; and this they began to do, and now all things will not fail (ἐκλείπω) from them whatever they set about doing; come and going down let us confound (συγχέω) there their tongue, so that they may not hear each the voice of his neighbour. And the Lord scattered them from there on the face of all the earth, and they ceased building the city and the tower. Therefore its name was called Confusion (Σύγχυσις), because there the Lord God confounded the lips of all the earth, and from there the Lord God scattered them on the face of all the earth.' And in the book entitled Wisdom of Solomon, about wisdom and the things at the confusion of tongues (διάλεκτος), in which the division of those on earth happened, such things are said about wisdom: 'She also, in the concord of wickedness (ὁμόνοια πονηρίας) of nations confounded, knew the righteous one and kept him blameless (ἄμεμπτος) to God and kept him strong against the compassion (σπλάγχνα) for a child.' Much and mystical is the account about these, to which fits: 'It is good to hide a king's mystery (μυστήριον βασιλέως κρύπτειν καλόν)'; so that the account (λόγος) about souls bound into (ἐνδέω) a body not from transmigration (μετενσωμάτωσις) may not be cast (ῥιπτέω) into chance ears, nor holy things be given 'to the dogs', nor pearls be thrown before swine. For such a thing is impious (ἀσεβής), containing betrayal (προδοσία) of the unspeakable oracles (ἀπόρρητα λόγια) of the wisdom of God, about which it is well written: 'Into an evil-scheming (κακότεχνος) soul wisdom will not enter, nor dwell in a body indebted (κατάχρεως) to sin.' It suffices to present things said hiddenly (κεκρυμμένως) as in the manner of history according to the manner of history, so that the able may work out (ἐπεξεργάζομαι) for themselves the things of the passage (τόπος).

pass_b_english: Celsus seems to me to have misheard certain more mystical teachings about how the things on earth were apportioned. Greek history too touches on these in some way, when it brings in some of those reputed to be gods contending with one another over Attica, and when in the poets it makes some of the so-called gods admit that certain places are more their own. Barbarian history also, and above all that of the Egyptians, shows something of the kind about the division of what are called the nomes of Egypt, saying that Athena, who obtained Sais by lot, is the same who also holds Attica. The learned men of the Egyptians will tell countless things of this sort, though I do not know whether they also include the Jews and their land when they assign lands to one being or another. But enough for the present about what is said on these matters outside the divine word.

We say that Moses, the prophet of God among us and his true servant, sets out in the song of Deuteronomy the following about the division of the earth: “When the Most High divided the nations, when he scattered the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the angels of God; and his people Jacob became the Lord’s portion, Israel the measured lot of his inheritance” (Deuteronomy 32:8–9).

And the same Moses, in the book entitled Genesis, tells of the division of the nations in the form of a history, as follows: “And all the earth had one language, and there was one speech for all. And it came to pass, as they moved from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they settled there” (Genesis 11:1–2). And a little after: “The Lord came down,” it says, “to see the city and the tower which the sons of men had built. And the Lord said: Behold, they are one race and all have one language; and this they have begun to do, and now nothing that they set out to do will fail them. Come, let us go down and confound their tongue there, so that none of them may understand the speech of his neighbour. And the Lord scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city and the tower. For this reason its name was called Confusion, because there the Lord God confounded the language of all the earth, and from there the Lord God scattered them over the face of all the earth” (Genesis 11:5–9).

And in the book entitled the Wisdom of Solomon, where it speaks of wisdom and of the events at the confusion of tongues, when the division of those on earth took place, this is said about wisdom: “She also, when the nations had been confounded in their agreement in wickedness, knew the righteous man, and kept him blameless before God, and kept him strong against his tender love for his child” (Wisdom of Solomon 10:5).

The teaching on these matters is long and mystical, and to it applies the saying, “It is good to keep hidden the secret of a king” (Tobit 12:7). This is so that the teaching about souls that are bound into a body, not by transmigration, may not be thrown to whatever ears happen to hear it, and what is holy may not be given “to the dogs,” nor pearls thrown before swine (Matthew 7:6). For such a thing is impious, since it means betraying the secret oracles of the wisdom of God, of which it is well written: “Wisdom will not enter a soul that plots evil, nor dwell in a body in debt to sin” (Wisdom of Solomon 1:4). It is enough to present in the manner of a history what is told in a hidden way as though it were history, so that those who are able may work out for themselves what bears on the passage.
notes: Deuteronomy 32:8 follows the LXX 'according to the number of the angels of God' (Hebrew/MT: 'sons of Israel'); kept as Origen reads it, since his argument rests on it. σχοίνισμα ('portion measured by line') rendered 'measured lot', kept the same in 5.31. Genesis 11 is quoted from the LXX: χεῖλος (literally 'lip') rendered 'language', φωνή 'speech'; ἀπ᾿ ἀνατολῶν kept as 'from the east' because Origen's allegory in 5.30-31 depends on it; Σύγχυσις ('Confusion') is the LXX's rendering of the name Babel; Origen skips Genesis 11:3-4 here ('a little after') and uses them in 5.30. The Wisdom of Solomon sentence has a doubled γῆς in the staged text (ὁ μερισμὸς τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, γῆς.), taken as dittography and translated once. Wisdom 10:5 refers to Abraham and Isaac; Origen's text reads ἐφύλαξεν where printed LXX has ἐτήρησεν in the first clause; sense unchanged. 'It is good to keep hidden the secret of a king' is Tobit 12:7 (also 12:11). 'Holy things to the dogs ... pearls before swine' is Matthew 7:6, given in Origen's own wording (παραβάλλωνται χοίροις). 'Our prophet of God and his true servant Moses' may echo Numbers 12:7 and Hebrews 3:5 (θεράπων); possible allusion only, not cited inline. Classical background left uncited because not certain from the Greek alone: the contest of Athena and Poseidon over Attica (told e.g. in Herodotus 8.55 and Apollodorus), gods in the poets naming favourite places (perhaps Hera's cities in Iliad 4.51-52), and the Greek identification of the goddess of Sais with Athena (compare Plato, Timaeus 21e). 'The teaching about souls bound into a body, though not by transmigration': ψυχῶν οὐκ ἐκ μετενσωματώσεως εἰς σῶμα ἐνδουμένων, translated literally; Origen distinguishes his view from transmigration. τινῶν in the first sentence taken with μυστικωτέρων λόγων ('certain teachings'), not as 'from certain people'.
